gc5.design_note: The path guard flags ANY change to a forbidden zone anywhere in <B1-base>..<cut-C>, regardless of which track's commit made it. Empirically confirmed 2026-09-03: this interval contains 451 changed files, including 95 under frontend/ and genuine B2 additions under api-gateway/.../presence/ and modifications to ReadOnlyEnforcementFilter.java -- because B1 and B2 share the same trunk and merge window. A flagged forbidden-zone hit is therefore evidence requiring an explicit reviewed disposition (see reviewed_exceptions), not an automatic B1 violation and not something this tool may silently wave through -- 'the file was already on main' / 'that was B2, not B1' reasoning is exactly the loophole the review warns against auto-applying. Also empirically confirmed: B1's OWN commits (Wave 0 62237deb, Wave 4b cab2814e, Wave 5b 0b5d60d1) touched files under frontend/, but only under frontend/tests/**, frontend/pacts/**, and playwright.config.ts (e2e specs, pact contracts, test helpers) -- never frontend/src/** (production UI). That is why the allowlist below distinguishes frontend test/contract infrastructure from frontend/src/**, rather than exempting frontend/ wholesale.
gc5.always_allowed_globs_note: Test fixtures and workflow/doc files per tasks.md's path-guard description ('an explicit allowlist (test fixtures, workflow files)'). A match here is never itself a violation, but does NOT exempt a file from the content guard -- a forbidden symbol inside an allowed-path file (e.g. a *Test.java under portfolio-service referencing the presence module) must still be caught, per Task C's own negative-fixture requirement.

enumeration_rules: Grep every src/main Java file repo-wide for: .save(, .saveAll(, .delete(, .deleteAll(, .deleteById(, JdbcTemplate/NamedParameterJdbcTemplate update(/execute( calls, and raw java.sql.Statement.executeUpdate( calls.
For each hit, confirm which table(s) it touches (via the containing SQL literal or the repository's entity type) and whether it lives in src/main (production) or src/test (fixture).

For every migration file (V1-V20), record every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/CREATE FUNCTION/DROP touching asset_holdings or portfolios, distinguishing a one-time historical statement from a persistent reusable function/trigger.

production_writers.mechanism: Line 79 portfolioRepository.saveAndFlush(new Portfolio(userId)) (INSERT, new user only, version=0 via DB DEFAULT). Lines 159-169 forceParentTransition: raw jdbcTemplate.update("UPDATE portfolios SET version = version + 1, updated_at = ... WHERE id = ? AND version = ?") -- the CAS itself. Lines 176-193 applyChildren: portfolio.getHoldings().clear()/addHolding() on a CascadeType.ALL/orphanRemoval=true collection, flushed at line 180 -- cascades to asset_holdings DELETE/INSERT, gated behind the successful CAS UPDATE in the same transaction.
replace() (lines 46-48) delegates 100% to HoldingReplacementService.replace(); own repository calls are read-only (portfolioRepository.findById).

seed() (lines 127-128) delegates 100% to HoldingReplacementService.replace(); javadoc states it deliberately never writes market_prices. Caller: PortfolioSeedController, compiled-in E2E_USER_ID = 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000e2e (PortfolioSeedController.java:25).

structural_risk_notes.note: asset_holdings.portfolio_id REFERENCES portfolios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE. Confirmed no production src/main code currently issues DELETE FROM portfolios or calls portfolioRepository.delete/deleteById anywhere -- the only DELETE-issuing call sites for either table in the whole tree are test fixtures (cleanup/isolation helpers, listed below) and the V17 repair function (R3, see unresolved). But this FK cascade itself is an unconditional, DB-level deletion mechanism with no version-CAS gate of its own: any future code path, admin script, or manual DB session that issues a portfolio-row DELETE would cascade-delete that portfolio's holdings outside HoldingReplacementService entirely, regardless of source-level guards. Not a current violation (nothing exercises it in production); documented as a structural gap for awareness, not something this checkpoint's tooling can close from source alone.

unresolved.summary: V17__Repair_Archive_And_Timestamp3.sql:58-156 defines repair_migrate_holdings(text,text,text), a persistent SQL function that mutates asset_holdings directly (UPDATE/DELETE by row id) with no portfolios.version CAS clause. V18/V19 invoke it for historical one-time migrations only (V18:13, V19:12); no DROP FUNCTION/REVOKE exists anywhere in tracked migrations or scripts, so it remains callable in any database built from the tracked migration history. The portfolios.version column itself is added only in V20, after V17-V19 ran, so the bypass was inert at migration-execution time -- the open risk is that the function remains callable post-V20/cutover with nothing in source preventing reinvocation outside the versioned write path.
unresolved.status: unresolved -- blocks 7.6/G6 acceptance per R3. A source-only review cannot establish live database privileges or prove the function unreachable; that requires a separate owner-authorized live/operational check. Do not resolve this by editing an already-applied Flyway migration or by silently excluding it from the writer inventory.

deployables.note: Roots are DERIVED from the build graph and validated against any declared list; a declared list that omits a derived root is a POLICY_INVALID finding, so an envelope cannot be narrowed without that narrowing itself being reviewed.
Bound separately: its JDBC insert into portfolios is a cross-deployable effect.

envelopes_note: EMPTY BY DESIGN. An envelope record attests that every member was analyzed, classified non-runtime, or reported unsupported (correction 7). That attestation is a human act; this tooling must never author one for itself. Until a reviewer writes these records, every deployable blocks with 'no reviewed envelope record' -- which is the correct state.
non_persistence_receiver_types_note: KafkaTemplate is deliberately ABSENT: it is message transport, not a generic non-persistence or in-memory type. It is classified store=transport so its outbound effect is described accurately rather than being flattened into 'in-memory'.
inactive_features_note: Configured-but-empty and UNAPPROVED (correction 10). A non-empty value here is ignored and produces a blocking POLICY_INVALID finding, so enabling one is a visible, separately-approved act.
evidence_binding_note: Task A/B evidence is supplied as a PER-RUN input via --run-input, never committed here -- committing a post-build hash would force a commit->rebuild cycle. See the runbook.
